Predicted values of PGLMM

Source: R/pglmm-utils.R
pglmm-predicted-values.Rd

pglmm_predicted_values calculates the predicted values of Y. By default, they are on the scale of the linear predictor (i.e. in the transformed space for the generalized linear mixed models with family %in% c("binomial","poisson")).

Usage

pglmm_predicted_values(
  x,
  cpp = TRUE,
  gaussian.pred = c("nearest_node", "tip_rm"),
  re.form = NULL,
  type = c("link", "response"),
  ...
)

communityPGLMM.predicted.values(
  x,
  cpp = TRUE,
  gaussian.pred = c("nearest_node", "tip_rm")
)

Arguments

x

A fitted model with class communityPGLMM.

cpp

Not used anymore.

gaussian.pred

When family is gaussian and bayes = FALSE, which type of prediction to calculate? Option nearest_node (default) gives the fitted values conditional on the estimated random effects (i.e. Xb + Zu, with u from ranef()), which is the same as fitted() or predict() of lme4. Option tip_rm gives leave-one-out predictions: each data point is removed, then predicted with the remaining ones (i.e. Xb plus the prediction of its residual given the residuals of all other data points).

re.form

(formula, NULL, or NA) specify which random effects to condition on when predicting. If NULL, include all random effects (i.e Xb + Zu); if NA or ~0, include no random effects (i.e. Xb).

type

Whether the predicted values are on the scale of the linear predictor ("link", default) or of the response ("response").

...

Optional additional parameters. None are used at present.

Value

A data frame with column Y_hat (predicted values accounting for both fixed and random terms, unless re.form is NA or ~0).

Examples

# community data: abundance of each species at each site
dat <- data.frame(
  site = rep(rownames(comm_a), times = ncol(comm_a)),
  sp = rep(colnames(comm_a), each = nrow(comm_a)),
  freq = unlist(comm_a, use.names = FALSE)
)
dat$shade <- envi$shade[match(dat$site, envi$site)]
phy <- ape::keep.tip(phylotree, unique(dat$sp))
fit <- pglmm(freq ~ shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site),
  data = dat, cov_ranef = list(sp = phy)
)

# fitted values conditional on the estimates of random effects: Xb + Zu
head(pglmm_predicted_values(fit))
#>      Y_hat
#> 1 2.884917
#> 2 3.434059
#> 3 3.747206
#> 4 2.857687
#> 5 3.695014
#> 6 4.384845
# leave-one-out predictions
head(pglmm_predicted_values(fit, gaussian.pred = "tip_rm"))
#>      Y_hat
#> 1 3.049463
#> 2 3.458816
#> 3 3.504640
#> 4 3.020680
#> 5 3.905766
#> 6 3.779392
# without random effects: Xb
head(pglmm_predicted_values(fit, re.form = NA))
#>       Y_hat
#> 1 0.2020856
#> 2 0.7512273
#> 3 1.0643741
#> 4 0.1748555
#> 5 1.0121830
#> 6 1.7020138

# binomial model: scale of the linear predictor (logit) or of the response
dat$pa <- as.numeric(dat$freq > 0)
fit_pa <- pglmm(pa ~ shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site),
  data = dat, family = "binomial", cov_ranef = list(sp = phy)
)
head(pglmm_predicted_values(fit_pa))
#>         Y_hat
#> 1 -0.56245900
#> 2 -0.15454887
#> 3  0.07806104
#> 4 -0.58268594
#> 5  0.03929272
#> 6  0.55170874
head(pglmm_predicted_values(fit_pa, type = "response"))
#>       Y_hat
#> 1 0.3629787
#> 2 0.4614395
#> 3 0.5195054
#> 4 0.3583148
#> 5 0.5098219
#> 6 0.6345319
